exercise2.prompt: Missing Markers on Load: The mean without the sentinel

hiddenCases.name: no sentinel leaves the mean alone
pandas does the reading
hiddenCases.describe: pd.read_csv rather than the answer typed in

exercise2.hint: na_values=[999] at load time turns the sentinel into NaN, and mean() skips NaN. Filtering with != 999 works too; naming it at load is the habit that scales.

questions.prompt: A file writes missing scores as "n/a". What happens if you do not say so?
questions.explain: One unconvertible value takes the whole column to object, and then sum concatenates instead of adding.

questions.prompt: Which argument names a file’s own missing markers?
questions.explain: It adds to the list pandas already knows, and doing it at load keeps the column numeric from the start.

choices: A count of missing values per column
questions.explain: isna gives a boolean frame, and summing a boolean column counts the Trues. Sum it twice for a single total.

questions.prompt: Why is a missing marker of 999 more dangerous than "n/a"?
choices: The column stays numeric, so nothing looks wrong and the mean is ruined
questions.explain: A text marker at least breaks the dtype and draws attention. A numeric sentinel is absorbed silently into every statistic.
